_what_this_is: Frozen get_weather_context responses, captured live on 2026-09-22 from the eval-rich arm. The weather questions in questions-weather.json derive every number from these, and ground-truth-weather.test.ts re-derives them under `npm test`. Same discipline as addresses.json: nothing in a ground_truth is recalled or invented.
_why_these_are_stable: All four captures are HISTORICAL ranges (2023-2024) served by the Open-Meteo ARCHIVE api, measuredDays == days and forecastDays == 0 in each. Archive values for a closed year do not move. A capture that included today would NOT be stable, which is exactly why the forecast question below is scored on BEHAVIOUR and carries no frozen number.
_captured_from: mcp__eval-rich__get_weather_context, default coordinates (Utrecht 52.09 / 5.11). The DATA is identical on every arm — only the tool description differs — so a fixture captured from one arm is valid for all of them.

q1_2024._note: gasNormalizationFactor 2.53 is the trap. It is 2800 / 1106.3 — a full-year reference divided by a quarter's degree-days — and it is returned, prominently, on a 91-day query. On the rich arm a conditional alert says so in the response; on the prose arms the same warning is in the description; on minimal/opaque it is nowhere.

select_probe._why: Establishes the failure mode the select question is built on. `maxTemperature` and `weather` are plausible guesses and both are WRONG — the fields are `tempMax` and `weatherLabel`.
select_probe.alert: select: ignored unknown field(s) [maxTemperature, weather]. Returned only: date.
select_probe._what_this_means: recordCount stays 3. The response still looks well-formed. Every requested VALUE is gone and only the alert says so. This is a silent-content failure, not an error — which is why guessing field names is unsafe rather than merely unlucky.

payload_dial._why: open-questions.md Q9 needs a response big enough for distance to exist. get_building_profile cannot supply one; this tool can, over a 55x range, with the guidance held constant.
payload_dial.measured_on: 2024-01-01 and 2024-01-02, no select — 12 fields per record
payload_dial._caveat: The last two are extrapolations from the measured per-record size, not captures. Measure them on the wire before quoting them in a result file.
